result:
I've added checks so that every issue, comment and project change can only point at things in its own workspace. The type check is clean and the existing test suite passes (617 tests), but I didn't add new tests for these four cases.

- **Assignees and project leads:** they must be current members of the workspace. That applies when creating an issue, reassigning one, creating a project and changing a project's lead. "Current" means an active member who hasn't left or been removed; someone who has been invited but not yet joined counts as not a member.
- **Labels:** when an issue is created or its labels change, each label must be one of that workspace's own. A label from another workspace is now filtered out when issues and lists are displayed, so labels already attached wrongly no longer show.
- **Parent issues:** the parent must be a live issue in the same project.
- **Replies:** a reply must be to a live, top-level comment on the same issue.
- **Mentions:** @handles and ids sent by the composer are both limited to current members; anyone else is silently dropped and never notified. Mention lookup used to scan only the first 100 members; it now covers the whole workspace.

A label, parent issue or reply target that belongs to another workspace raises the same error as any other cross-workspace access. Everything else that fails (missing, archived, deleted, not a member, wrong project, reply to a reply) is refused as not found. All checks run before anything is written, so a refused change creates nothing and sends no notification.

The shared checks are in a new file, `src/server/services/_references.ts`. They are called from the issue, comment and project services. I also added lookups that can see other workspaces' records, used only to tell "belongs elsewhere" apart from "doesn't exist", to the label, issue and comment repositories.
